APCTT-C01.quote: ADCIRC computes wind and wave driven storm surges within the region of interest and SWAN computes wind-driven wave fields (Toro and others, 2011).
APCTT-C01.note: Physical basis: coupled hydrodynamic surge and wave models, contrasted with the bathtub method (p12, p18).

APCTT-C02.quote: The purpose of these map libraries is to estimate varying degrees of flood-inundation scenarios and provide visualizations to help users understand the coastal flood risk in each area.
APCTT-C02.note: Application for emergency managers and residents, linked to real-time gages and NWS forecasts (p11).

APCTT-C03.quote: Utilizing the time series output of water-surface elevation from a hydrodynamic model and relating the simulated and measured water-surface elevation at each of the 25 U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) tide gage and map extents, allowed for the development of storm driven inundation maps linked to 25 USGS real-time tide gages along the coast of New Jersey.
APCTT-C03.note: Analytical results: map libraries of extent and depth per gage stage.

APCTT-C05.quote: The simulated peak for the event matched the historical peak with a reasonable difference of approximately 1 ft.
APCTT-C05.note: Model output compared with recorded tide data at the gages and with FEMA flood-hazard zones (qualitative, p38); FEMA calibration accepted (p32).

APCTT-C06.quote: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), in cooperation with the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) and the New Jersey Office of Emergency Management (NJOEM), created digital flood-inundation maps for approximately 1,430 square miles of the New Jersey coast and tidewaters through 10 coastal counties stretching from Cumberland County through Bergen County, New Jersey.
APCTT-C06.note: Maps produced for the real study area.

APCTT-C07.quote: This study developed an online user interface to allow the coastal flood inundation maps for each of the 25 USGS tide gages to be seen by the public.
APCTT-C07.note: Maps served publicly in the FDST web tool, linked to real-time gage pages and NWS forecasts: actual operational setting.

APCTT-C08.note: No qualification against stated requirements; uncertainty flags and limitations instead.

APCTT-C09.note: The maps are newly published; no record of use over a period.

APCTT-C10.quote: The simulated peak for the event matched the historical peak with a reasonable difference of approximately 1 ft.
APCTT-C10.note: Criterion stated on the same page: differences less than 2 ft indicate good agreement.

APCTT-C11.quote: The water elevation time-series was output on a 400-second timestep for the FEMA model used for this study and was the output used to generate the flood inundation maps described within this report.
APCTT-C11.note: Two synthetic storms per gage, 9 to 30 stages per gage, model output and DEM described.

APCTT-C12.quote: The flood-inundation maps can be accessed through the USGS Interagency Flood Risk Management (InFRM) Flood Decision Support Toolbox (FDST).
APCTT-C12.note: The evidence is about the inundation maps in FDST themselves.
